claims.claim: Natural springs are a different proposition from venues that heat and mineralise their water artificially.
claims.note: General contextual statement, not a checkable fact.

claims.claim: The source does the work: geothermal energy or mineral-rich aquifer water rises to the surface, and the venue builds around it.
claims.note: General explanatory statement about how natural springs work.

claims.claim: What you get in the water is genuinely the product of geology instead of a recipe.
claims.note: Editorial/atmospheric claim, not checkable from venue records.

claims.claim: The Great Artesian Basin feeds bore baths scattered across outback Queensland and New South Wales
claims.note: General geographic/geological context not verifiable from venue records alone, though Eulo (QLD) and Pilliga (NSW) are consistent with this.

claims.claim: Places like the Artesian Mud Baths in Eulo or the Pilliga Artesian Bore Bath are working-class infrastructure in the oldest sense: communities built around free or very cheap access to water
claims.note: Characterisation/atmosphere; cost field for Artesian Mud Baths is null, Pilliga has a camping fee only, so 'free or very cheap' is partially supported but partly unverifiable.

claims.claim: The Pilliga bath runs around the clock, every day
with a campsite attached instead of a day-pass counter
claims.note: cost field references a camping fee, implying campsite; no day-pass pricing listed.

claims.claim: Peninsula Hot Springs and Alba Thermal Springs have both scaled into large multi-pool complexes
claims.note: No field in the records describes scale or number of pools; cannot be verified or contradicted.

claims.claim: Mineral Springs Hotel in Hepburn Springs adds a sauna and cold plunge to its spring-fed indoor pool
claims.note: amenities show traditional_sauna: true, cold_plunge: true; facilities show indoor_pool: true, natural_spring: true.

claims.claim: which sets it apart from the purely thermal venues in this table
Deep Blue in Warrnambool runs structured sessions instead of open entry
claims.note: hours field lists named sessions (9:30am, 12pm, 2:30pm, twilight 7:30–9:30pm).

claims.claim: so it's worth checking timing before you turn up
claims.note: Editorial advice, not a checkable fact.

claims.claim: Woodlands Rainforest Retreat in Narbethong packages its springs access with massage and dining instead of selling entry alone
claims.note: cost field describes a package including bathing, couples massage and Japanese Charcoal BBQ.

claims.claim: The swimwear-optional dress code is also worth knowing ahead of time.
A few venues haven't published drop-in prices here, so the table will show that plainly instead of us guessing.
claims.note: Meta-statement about table behaviour resolved by components; not a prose factual claim.

claims.claim: Hours vary considerably across the set
claims.note: Hours fields across venues range from 24-hour open to narrow session windows, confirming variation.

claims.claim: a handful of venues operate without bookings, which is rarer than it used to be
claims.note: The 'rarer than it used to be' part is a historical claim unverifiable from records; the 'without bookings' part is consistent with bookings_required: false across all listed venues.

claims.claim: Victoria's springs country, centred on the Mornington Peninsula and the Daylesford-Hepburn region
claims.note: General geographic characterisation; venue records confirm VIC venues in those areas but 'centred on' is editorial.
